what_this_is: An LLM invented the scenarios; code retrieved real 2013-2024 company-months that matched their OBSERVABLE fields; realised value-weighted excess returns graded matched-vs-control, paired by month block. No scenario ever received an invented return.

event_type.note: 8-K item codes stand in for the event taxonomy via EIGHTK_ITEM_EVENT_TYPE. Availability = EDGAR acceptance timestamp, never the event's own date. Not a retrieval predicate yet: the tape is survivor-tilted (current registrants only) and not panel-joined.

sector_theme.note: the free-text theme itself; only its division hint maps

falsifier.note: not a retrieval field -- it is what a future test would look for, recorded so the scenario is refutable at all

backoff.why: a five-way conjunction of quantile bands cuts a sector to a few dozen name-months; the ladder drops the least central predicate until the floor is met and NAMES what it dropped. Two scenarios at different levels answer different questions -- the ranking does not equate them.

llm_disagreement.reading: Agreement is NOT correctness -- two models agreeing that demand rose says the concept is easy to guess, not that it rose. What matters is WHERE they agree: if the predicate fields agree far less than the narrative fields, then the analogue set a scenario retrieves is substantially an artefact of which model was asked, and every spread in this receipt inherits that.

unmappable_concepts.reads_as: each row is a concept the LLM used that this panel cannot express. This IS the next data-acquisition list, in priority order by count.

ranked_at_declared_horizon.mechanism: A new technology standard makes the incumbent's large installed base of machines non-compliant, causing customers to defer replacement parts and service, reducing recurring revenue and forcing write-downs.

A surge in orders for next-generation jet engines outpaces the foundry's ability to add casting capacity, so the bottleneck holder gains pricing power and long-term supply agreements, improving its future returns.

As the bank tightens underwriting standards and reduces loan origination for commercial property projects, developers cancel or delay new construction, cutting demand for the company's property-management and leasing services, which lowers occupancy and fee income.

End customers increasingly prefer smaller, local, and value-oriented shopping trips, causing foot traffic and basket sizes at large-format retail stores to decline, which reduces their sales and margins.
Flooding halts underground ore extraction, reducing the incumbent's output and forcing it to buy higher-cost ore on the spot market, eroding margins until the mine is dewatered and repaired.

A large retail customer shifts its wholesale purchasing to a national distributor with lower logistics costs, causing the incumbent regional wholesaler to lose recurring volume and pricing power, leading to margin compression and underperformance.

A major industrial assembler substitutes a cheaper, higher-performing composite material for the incumbent supplier's specialty alloy in a high-volume product line, reducing orders and eroding the supplier's market share and pricing power.

A regional assembler relocates its component sourcing to a lower-cost region, reducing orders to the incumbent domestic supplier, whose fixed cost base remains, compressing margins and future cash flows.

A spike in diesel costs raises cash operating costs per tonne for all miners, but the company with a high strip ratio and long haul distances sees a disproportionate cost increase, compressing its margin and forcing it to either cut output or accept lower profitability, while lower-strip-ratio peers absorb the shock and gain relative cost advantage.
A major national parcel carrier halts service to certain regions due to a labor dispute, so the retailer's online orders cannot be delivered, causing sales to drop and inventory to pile up.

A regulatory shift removes licensing barriers, allowing many new service providers to enter the market, increasing supply and intensifying competition, which erodes the incumbent's pricing power and market share.

A competing regional mall is acquired and closed, reducing total retail space in the trade area, which shifts foot traffic and tenant demand to the surviving mall owner, boosting its lease rates and occupancy.

A multi-year exclusivity agreement that locked in a major corporate client expires, allowing rival service providers to bid for the contract, eroding the incumbent's revenue and margins as pricing competition intensifies.
A new entrant with a leaner cost structure undercuts the incumbent's prices, stealing market share and forcing the incumbent to cut prices, compressing margins and eroding future cash flows.

A step change in grid electricity tariffs raises the variable cost of operating electric-vehicle charging networks, compressing margins for the service provider until it can pass through the cost to customers.

A new emissions standard mandates that operators replace aging diesel fleets within a fixed window, creating a surge of orders for compliant locomotives while the incumbent supplier's production capacity is already tight, driving higher future returns through volume and pricing power.

A regional shortage of certified steel erectors and welders forces general contractors to queue projects, so a specialized steel erection firm with an experienced crew can command higher utilization and pricing for its constrained output.

Customers accelerate purchases ahead of an announced import tariff or regulatory deadline, pulling forward demand that would otherwise occur later, creating a temporary order boom that inflates current earnings and expectations, after which orders collapse as the pulled-forward demand is exhausted.
